audit.whatIsWrong: late claims "your Granite Shield plus tankiness mean his passive execute never triggers", and early says "His passive heals harder the lower you are".
audit.why: Eternal Hunger is not an execute and it does not read your health at all. It heals WARWICK when HE is below 50%, tripled below 25%. Both lines invert the mechanic: they tell you your own HP bar controls his passive when it is his HP bar that does, which turns the single most important rule of the matchup — do not let a low Warwick keep fighting — into its opposite. The thing your health bar actually controls is Blood Hunt, which only senses enemies under 50%.
audit.corrected: Eternal Hunger described as his own low-health heal; the 50% threshold reassigned to Blood Hunt in early, late, wants.foe[1] and whys[6].
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (P "If Warwick is below 50% health, he heals the same amount. If Warwick is below 25% health, this healing triples."; W "senses enemies below 50% health")

audit.whatIsWrong: Blood Hunt is described only as "W move speed" with no trigger condition, and Infinite Duress is treated as a fixed-range flank.
audit.why: Blood Hunt activates on enemies under 50% health — above that line it gives him nothing against you. And Infinite Duress "leaps in a direction, scaling with his bonus Move Speed", so the Blood Hunt speed literally lengthens his ultimate's travel. Chained together that is one actionable rule the entry never states: stay above half health and you shrink both his approach speed and his ult range at the same time. It also makes the 1.5-second suppress the thing to respect, not a generic "lock".
audit.corrected: The 50% threshold and the R-range-scales-with-move-speed chain added to mid, wants.foe[1], whys[4] and whys[6].
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (W "senses enemies below 50% health, gaining Move Speed toward"; R "leaps in a direction (scaling with his bonus Move Speed), suppressing the first champion he collides with for 1.5 seconds")

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemisation advice is armour, armour, armour: "Itemize armor and you simply outlast him", "Every armor item makes E and W hit harder while shrinking his auto-attack drain to nothing".
audit.why: Two problems the kit is explicit about. Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the target's MAXIMUM HEALTH — a Malphite who answers by stacking health and armour is feeding the one ability that ignores the plan. And three separate sources of healing (Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast, Infinite Duress) mean the extended trade the entry wants you to win is decided by Grievous Wounds, which is never mentioned once. Armour is still correct against his autos; it is just not the whole answer, and the page currently sells it as one.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in spikes[3], late and whys[5]; the max-health caveat added so armour is framed as the answer to his autos, not to Q.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (Q "dealing damage based on their maximum health and healing for damage dealt")

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere. "Hold R to cancel his R suppress-flank" gives no sense of how often either ultimate comes back.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70 against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100 — Warwick's ultimate is back first at every single rank, by 20 to 30 seconds. That inverts the usual tank read: you do not get to trade ultimates evenly with him, so spending R to answer a suppress is a losing exchange over the course of a game unless it wins the fight outright. Primal Howl's 15-to-11-second fear is the other timer, and it is the thing that will interrupt your follow-up after you land R.
audit.corrected: Ultimate cooldowns compared in spikes[2] and whys[4]; Primal Howl named with its cooldown in mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Malphite Level 2 and Level 3, but spikes[0] labels "Lvl 1-2" Warwick's window, early says "At Levels 1-3 you have no trade pattern", and whys[0] and whys[1] both describe Warwick winning those stages.
audit.why: Four fields on the same page say Warwick owns the opening and the chart says Malphite does. The prose is right — Malphite has no Thunderclap, and Jaws of the Beast on a 8-second cooldown with a heal attached is a real level-2 threat. The chart is what is wrong, and it is the first thing a player reads.
audit.corrected: Level 2 to Warwick, Level 3 to Skill; levels 6 and beyond stay Malphite, which the 55.19% win rate over 877 games supports.

edits.before: Respect him here — this is the one window Warwick beats you. At Levels 1-3 you have no trade pattern and your Granite Shield just gets chewed by his bloodlust autos while his Q heals back anything you poke with Seismic Shard. Don't sit in his auto range trying to trade; last-hit at max Q range, keep the shield up by disengaging, and farm. His passive heals harder the lower you are, so never let him drag you to half HP for an extended fight before you have W.
edits.after: Respect him here — this is the one window Warwick beats you. At Levels 1-3 you have no trade pattern and Granite Shield just gets chewed while Jaws of the Beast, an 8-second bite off your max health, heals back anything Seismic Shard chips in. Don't sit in his auto range; last-hit at max Q range, disengage to recharge the shield, and farm. Eternal Hunger heals HIM harder the lower HE is, so never leave a half-health Warwick alive in a trade you started.

edits.before: The lane flips to you here. W Thunderclap gives you bonus armor and AoE splash autos, and E Ground Slam slashes his attack speed — which is where almost all of Warwick's damage and his Q-heal input come from. Land E into a W-empowered auto trade and his drain falls apart. At 6, R is the answer to everything: it's unstoppable so his W move speed can't kite it, it cancels his all-in, and it lets you flip a fight if he tries to R-suppress a teammate.
edits.after: The lane flips to you here. Thunderclap gives bonus armor and splash autos, and Ground Slam slashes the attack speed almost all of his damage rides on. Land E into a W-empowered auto and his drain falls apart — but expect Primal Howl, a 15-second fear that eats your follow-up before it lands. At 6, the rule is your health bar: Blood Hunt only senses you under 50%, and Infinite Duress leaps further the faster he moves, so staying above half shortens his ult.

edits.before: You own this. Every armor item makes E and W hit harder while shrinking his auto-attack drain to nothing, and your Granite Shield plus tankiness mean his passive execute never triggers. He stays a chase threat in skirmishes, so don't get caught alone at low HP where his heal snowballs — but in any extended fight or sidelane 1v1, your E attack-speed slow turns him into a non-threat and your R is a free pick or peel. Itemize armor and you simply outlast him.
edits.after: You own this, with one correction to the plan. Armor makes Ground Slam hit harder and shrinks his autos, but Jaws of the Beast reads your MAXIMUM health, so stacking HP feeds the one ability armor cannot touch. Buy Grievous Wounds: three of his abilities heal him, and the extended fight this matchup always becomes is decided there. Don't get caught under 50% where Blood Hunt turns on — above that line, E-slow him and your R is a free pick or peel.

notes: Two things I could not resolve from the kit and therefore did not write. (1) Whether Primal Howl's fear can interrupt Unstoppable Force mid-dash — the fear is hard CC and the R is described only as "launches himself to a location at high speed", with needsResearch empty, so I stated that Primal Howl eats your follow-up rather than claiming anything about the dash itself. (2) Whether Malphite's knock-up interrupts the Infinite Duress channel; the kit flags R as a channel but says nothing about interruptibility, so the existing suggestion that your R "answers his suppress flank" was replaced with a cooldown argument instead of an interaction claim. Also carried forward from the Zac mirror: Malphite's Q and E carry a "grounding" flag that is a tooltip-parsing artefact of the words "through the ground" and "slams the ground" — neither ability grounds, and I wrote nothing based on it.
